texts.preamble: Alisab Fakir/Shaikh vs Shahebjankhan S-O Haji Abdul ...
texts.facts: The present appeals are filed by the original claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the common judgment and award dated 20.04.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi), Vadodara in MACP Nos.1515, 1516 and 1517 of 1993. The brief facts of the case is that the on 23.04.1993, the deceased and injured persons were traveling by a truck no. AET/7205, which was being driven by Alisab at a moderate speed while proceeding towards Ahmedabad. When the said truck reached near place of occurrence, a truck NO. CAM/6668 came from opposite direction i.e.,from Ahmedabad side in rash and negligent manner and in attempting to overtake the foregoing truck, the truck No.CAM/6668 came on wrong side and dashed with the truck No.AET/7205. Because of heavy impact, both the trucks dashed against each other and both the drivers as well as trucks caught fire. Hence, they have filed the abovementioned petitions to claim compensation from the respondents jointly and severally. The MACP Nos.1515 and 1516 of 1993 (First Appeal Nos. 121 and 122 of 2014) were originally filed seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- on account of the death of deceased and MACP No.1517 of 1993 (First Appeal No.3107 of 2014) was originally filed seeking compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- on account of the injuries received in the motor-vehicular accident. 3. Vide the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petitions preferred by the present appellant - original claimant under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the present appellant- original claimant entitled to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined Rs.2,64,800/-, Rs.5,38,400/- and Rs.1,46,900/- in MACP Nos.1515/93, 1516/93 and 1517/93 respectively at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petitions till its actual realization with proportionate costs. All the respondents - original opponents are held jointly and severally liable to pay such enhanced amount of compensation with proportionate costs and interest. First Appeal no.122 of 2013 19. As regards the income is concerned, in the present appeal also, the claimant was engaged in the occupation of the driver. Sofar as contention with regard to the income of the appellant is concerned, It is stated that the appellant was working as a cleaner and earning Rs.1500/- per month and other allowances. The appellant has produced salary certificate at exhibit 82, in which income of Rs.2000/- per month + Rs.40/- bhattha was stated. 26. The appellant has produced the disability certificates issued by Dr. Sunil Paradkar and Dr. Munish Shah at exhibits 35 and 32 respectively. The disability in the eye was assessed as 75%.
texts.arguments: Learned advocate Mr. Mohsin Hakim, appearing for the appellants, while assailing the impugned judgment, has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation to the claimants and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true perspective. 6. The first contention is raised with regard to the issue of negligency in MACP No.121 of 2014. It is submitted that the tribunal has held the deceased for contributory negligency of 50% and thereby reduced the compensation awardable to that extent. It is further argued that the tribunal has failed to appreciate the fact that the owner of the vehicle had secured his employee-driver by paying extra premium in the event that even if the driver suffers any injury or expires because of his own negligence, insurance company is liable to pay the amount as per the M V Act. In First Appeal Nos.121 and 122 of 2014, It is contended by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the Tribunal has erred while considering the income of the deceased only Rs.2000/- per month and bhathha of Rs.600/-. The tribunal has not appreciated the evidence produced at exhibit 81 i.e., the salary certificate, which shows that the deceased was earning Rs.8300/- per month. It is argued that the income of the deceased is required to be assessed on the basis of salary certificate produced on record. To substantiate his argument on the income aspect, he has placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of (I) Mohd. Ameeruddin and Another Vs. United India Insuraunce Company Ltd and Anr (2011) 1 Supreme Court Cases 304 and (II) Rajwati @ Rajjo Vs. United India Insurance Company Ltd with Seema Vs. United India Insurance Company Ltd 2022 (0) AIJEL SC 70210. It is further argued that the tribunal has overlooked the settled principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in relation to the assessment of future prospects, dependency, and grant of compensation under conventional heads such as loss of consortium, loss of estate, and funeral expenses. 8. So far as First Appeal No.3107 of 2014 is concerned, the main contentions were raised regarding the disability aspect. It is submitted by the learned Counsel that the claimant has suffered NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined grievous injuries such as multiple glass chip injuries over face, CLW over (Rt.) orbital region, Cheek, right side face and 1st and 2nd degree burns over face, chest and both the eye balls of the injured became white to some extent and the claimant cannot shut the eye lids in normal way and vision in right side is reduced to 25% and 35% in left eye i.e., total disablement in each eye is 75% and same is not curable and hence, the tribunal ought to have considered 100% functional disability. It is further argued that the tribunal has not properly considered the deposition of Dr. Munish Shah at exh.61, who has opined that because of the burn injury on the left hand fingures and thumb and wrist have stiffed and has sustained 90% disability and the claimant would not be able to work as cleaner. Learned Counsel has further placed reliance on the decision of Hon'ble Supreeme Court in the case of Jayanandan Vs. Varkey reported in 2024 (0) AIJEL-SC 75068. That, the tribunal has not considered the amount of bhattha as a part of salary and submitted that income should have been considered as per the salary certificate produced on record. Further, the tribunal has failed to award compensation for future medical expenses considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant. It is further argued that the tribunal has overlooked the settled principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in relation to the assessment of future loss of income including future prospect, multiplier, actual loss of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined income and grant of compensation under other heads such as PSS, Special diet and transportation and medical expenses. 9. Finally, It is submitted that the Tribunal has awarded a meager and unrealistic amount under various heads without considering the financial dependency of the family members and the socio- economic background of the appellant. The learned counsel has urged that the compensation awarded is not just, fair, and reasonable, and is liable to be enhanced in accordance with the settled legal principles. Learned counsel therefore prays for enhancement of the compensation amount by reassessing the same in accordance with law. Per contra learned Advocate Mr. G C Mazmudar and Learned advocate Mr. Palak Thakkar appearing for the respondent nos.2 and 4 respectively have placed reliance upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and vehemently argued that the compensation must be awarded as just, proper and reasonable and not higher side and further submitted that learned Tribunal, after appreciating the materials available on record, awarded the compensation under each head is just, proper and reasonable and not required to interfere and lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal. Sofar as the contention raised with regard to the issue of negligency, the Tribunal, while deciding the issue of negligence, has recorded a finding of 50% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and 50% negligence of the driver of the opponent vehicle, relying upon the complaint, coupled with panchnama and oral evidence of the injured witness ie. the appellant in First Appeal No.3107 of 2014 and other materials on record. Considering the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay Vs. Laxman Iyer and Anr reported in (2003) 8 Supreme Court Cases 731, it is well settled that in the case of contributory negligence, courts have power to apportion the loss between the parties as seems just and equitable. However, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 noticing the age of the deceased as 25 years, as accepted by the Tribunal, 40% amount can be considered towards the future prospects of the deceased. Considering the fact that the deceased was survived three dependents, as per the ration laid down in the decision of Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, 1/3th deduction is required to be applied towards spend by the deceased on himself. Thus, the calculation of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined prospective income of the deceased at the rate of 25% is considered as Rs.3500/- * 40% (Rs.1400)= Rs.4900/-. After 1/3th deduction towards personal expense of the deceased, the calculation of the income the deceased is Rs.3266/-(Rs.4900/- - Rs.1633/- (1/3th deduction towards personal expenses). 15. Noticing the fact that the deceased was aged 25 years at the time of accident, in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. (supra) and the scheduled prescribed, multiplier of 18 is required to be taken instead of 17 applied by the tribunal. Thus, the future loss benefit is determined as Rs.3266/-*12*18 (Multiplier) which comes to Rs.7,05,456/-. 16. As rightly prayed for by the learned advocate for the appellant in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhur Ram & Ors reported in (2018)18 SCC 130, the claimants would be entitled to enhance amount of compensation under the head of loss of consortium to the tune of Rs.1,45,200/- (Rs.48,400/- X 3). However, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 noticing the age of the deceased as 35 years as per the PM Report, as accepted by the Tribunal, 40% amount can be considered towards the future prospects of the deceased. Considering the fact that the deceased was survived by four dependents, as per the ration laid down in the decision of Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, 1/4th deduction is required to be applied towards spend by the deceased on himself. As rightly prayed for by the learned advocate for the appellant in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhur Ram & Ors reported in (2018)18 SCC 130, the claimants would be entitled to enhance amount of compensation under the head of loss of consortium to the tune of Rs.1,93,600/- (Rs.48,400/- X 4). Therefore, it is the duty of the Court to place victim close as possible to their pre-accident lives and therefore, considering the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pappu Deo Yadav V. Naresh Kumar and ors reported in 2020 ACJ 2695 and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 noticing the age of the deceased as 30 years Thus, the income would be (Rs.1500*40%=600) Rs.2100/- after the calculation of the future rise. 28. Noticing the fact that the deceased was aged 30 years at the time of accident, in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and the scheduled prescribed, the Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier of 17.
